Eviction Policy

1. What is an Eviction Policy?
  • An eviction policy controls which entries to remove when memory is running low;
  • It is different from expiry — expiry removes entries after a time duration; eviction removes entries based on memory pressure;
  • Eviction is configured at the data region level (not at the cache level);
2. Page-Based Eviction
  • Ignite evicts data at the page level, not at the individual entry level;
  • When a data region reaches its maximum size, Ignite starts evicting the least recently used pages;
  • Two eviction modes:
    • RANDOM_LRU — randomly samples pages and evicts the least recently used among the sample;
    • RANDOM_2_LRU — uses two random samples for better LRU approximation (slightly more CPU);
3. Configuring Eviction
  • Eviction is enabled by setting the max size on a data region and choosing an eviction mode: 
    DataRegionConfiguration regionCfg = new DataRegionConfiguration();
regionCfg.setName("myRegion");
regionCfg.setInitialSize(100L * 1024 * 1024);   // 100 MB initial
regionCfg.setMaxSize(500L * 1024 * 1024);        // 500 MB max
regionCfg.setPageEvictionMode(DataPageEvictionMode.RANDOM_LRU);

DataStorageConfiguration storageCfg = new DataStorageConfiguration();
storageCfg.setDataRegionConfigurations(regionCfg);

IgniteConfiguration igniteCfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
igniteCfg.setDataStorageConfiguration(storageCfg);
  • Assign a cache to a specific data region: 
    CacheConfiguration cacheCfg = new CacheConfiguration("myCache");
cacheCfg.setDataRegionName("myRegion");
4. On-Heap Cache (Near Cache Eviction)
  • Ignite also supports on-heap caching via Near Cache with entry-level eviction policies;
  • Near cache eviction policies: LRU (Least Recently Used) and FIFO (First In First Out); 
    NearCacheConfiguration nearCfg = new NearCacheConfiguration();
nearCfg.setNearEvictionPolicy(new LruEvictionPolicy(10_000)); // keep 10K entries max

CacheConfiguration cacheCfg = new CacheConfiguration("myCache");
cacheCfg.setNearConfiguration(nearCfg);
5. Eviction vs. Expiry vs. Persistence
MechanismTriggerData Recovery
EvictionMemory pressure (region full)Re-loaded from persistence/CacheStore
ExpiryTime duration elapsedGone permanently
PersistenceN/A — data stored on diskAvailable after restart
